title: Substrate-induced crystallisation in polymers: Exceptional impact of prefreezing versus heterogeneous nucleation on kinetics and morphology
authors: Marthinus van Niekerk, Muhammad Tariq, Oleksandr Dolynchuk
abstract: Crystallisation of liquids often occurs at solid surfaces, via heterogeneous nucleation or prefreezing. Understanding this process is crucial for controlling crystal morphology in thin films and developing efficient nucleating agents - especially for polymers, typically processed in a molten state. However, the efficiency of nucleation and prefreezing with respect to crystallisation kinetics and semicrystalline polymer morphology has not been well studied and remains unclear. Here, we address this challenge by conducting a systematic study of substrate-induced crystallisation in dewetted droplets of the model polymer poly($\varepsilon$-caprolactone) (PCL) on various crystalline and amorphous substrates. Using polarized light optical microscopy, droplet crystallisation temperature was monitored and varied across the substrates, revealing three scenarios: close-to-homogeneous nucleation on glass and silicon; heterogeneous nucleation on ordered and disordered carbon-rich substrates; and prefreezing on graphene. The temperature-dependent nucleation rate was analysed and found to obey classical nucleation theory for all systems except PCL on graphene, where it diverges as all the droplets crystallise simultaneously. The highest in- and out-of-plane PCL crystal orientation is found on graphene, where the epitaxially grown lamellae extend vertically over several hundred nanometres. These results demonstrate that prefreezing has a superior influence on crystallisation kinetics and crystal morphology, making prefreezing substrates perfect nucleating agents.
summary: This work investigates how crystallization in polymers is initiated on different surfaces by comparing prefreezing and heterogeneous nucleation mechanisms. By studying PCL on various substrates, the authors demonstrate that prefreezing provides a superior pathway for controlling crystal growth kinetics and achieving highly oriented crystal structures. This has significant implications for materials science applications requiring controlled polymer morphology.
main_problem: The study aims to systematically compare the influence of prefreezing versus heterogeneous nucleation on the kinetics and resulting morphology of substrate-induced crystallization in polymers.
main_result: Prefreezing was shown to have a superior influence on crystallization kinetics and crystal morphology compared to heterogeneous nucleation, suggesting prefreezing substrates are excellent nucleating agents.
method: The researchers used polarized light optical microscopy (PLOM) and quantitative analysis of temperature-dependent nucleation rates, comparing crystallization behavior on various crystalline and amorphous substrates.
model_or_system: The physical system involves the crystallization of the model polymer poly(epsilon-caprolactone) (PCL) within dewetted droplets deposited on diverse substrates, including graphene, glass, and silicon.
key_observables: Crystallization temperature (Tc), nucleation rate per area, and in- and out-of-plane crystal orientation.
important_parameters: Interfacial energies ($\gamma$), supercooling ($\Delta T$), and the comparison between equilibrium (prefreezing) and non-equilibrium (heterogeneous) processes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing kinetic models (like Classical Nucleation Theory) across different physical regimes (prefreezing vs. heterogeneous nucleation).
figures_summary: Figures show PLOM images monitoring crystallization, and data plots analyze the temperature dependence of the nucleation rate, revealing distinct kinetic regimes for different substrates.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares three crystallization scenarios (homogeneous, heterogeneous, prefreezing) across various substrates, analyzing kinetics via nucleation rate fits and morphology via microscopy and scattering techniques.
why_interesting: While focused on polymer physics, the detailed analysis of phase transitions, nucleation kinetics, and the comparison between equilibrium and non-equilibrium pathways touches upon fundamental concepts in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
